chitchat: Shut it behind you. The cold in here is doing a job.
Four hundred and six. It was four hundred and eleven.
Don't breathe on an open drawer.
Some of these haven't been grown in ninety years.
They aren't ours. We're just where they are.
description: A small precise man in a coat and fingerless gloves, working along a bank of drawers with a slate and a stub of chalk, counting under his breath in tens. He's very cold and doesn't appear to have thought about it in years.

bye.text:
"Mind how you go."

He goes back to the drawers.

options.label: Are you taking all this with you?

lock.text:
"No."

He writes a number, checks it, and writes it again.

"If it needed one it would be the wrong place for it."

root.first: "Shut the door." Then, having looked at you: "Thank you. Most people do not, first time."

options.label: There's no lock on the door.
Are you taking all this with you?

text_by_relation.close: He hands you the slate without looking up, and carries on counting, and you find you're keeping the tally.

options.label: There's no lock on the door.

taking.text:
He stops.

It is the first time he has stopped.

"Yes," he says, and there's a very long pause, and then he goes back to the drawers and says, in a completely ordinary voice, "That's what it was always for."

Somewhere above you, out in the compound, a great many people stop doing something at the same moment.

clothing_layers: a wool coat worn indoors, always

name: Preserved Wain
